questions.stem: Which is the most common subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nodular sclerosis is the most common type of Hodgkin's lymphoma, while mixed cellularity is most common in India.

The incidence of nodular sclerosis is equal in men and women. It commonly involves the lower cervical, supraclavicular, and mediastinal lymph nodes. It commonly affects adolescents and young adults. It has an excellent prognosis.

Mixed-cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma is seen in patients older than 50 years of age. There is a male predominance.

The image given below shows the histology of nodular sclerosis showing a lacunar variant of Reed–Sternberg cells






Robbins Basic Pathology, 10th Edition, Page no: 474

questions.stem: A lymph node biopsy specimen of a patient shows giant cells with an owl-eyed appearance. Which of the following statements is incorrect with respect to the diagnosis in this case?

options.label: A
options.text: Single axial group of lymph nodes is affected

options.label: B
options.text: Spleen is the first extranodal tissue to be involved

questions.solutionHtml:
An owl-eyed appearance of giant cells in lymph nodes is characteristic of Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL). Mesenteric lymph nodes are infrequently involved in HL.

Hodgkin’s lymphoma is a group of lymphoid neoplasms arising in a single group of lymph nodes. Extranodal involvement is uncommon. However, if it spreads from the nodes, the first organ to be involved is the spleen, then the liver, and finally the bone marrow. This pattern of spread is known as the contiguous spread.

This predictable route of spread is important clinically as it aids in staging and prognosis as well as treatment of HL. 





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 607

questions.stem: Activation of which of the following is a common event in classical Hodgkin's lymphoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Activation of the transcription factor NF-κB is a common event in classical Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL).

NF-κB may be activated by Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) infection. EBV+ tumor cells express latent membrane protein-1 (LMP-1) which upregulates NF-κB. Activation of NF-κB may occur in EBV tumors as a result of the acquired loss-of-function mutations in TNF alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3).

Activation of NF-κB by EBV rescues crippled germinal center B cells that cannot express Igs from apoptosis, eventually leading to the formation of Reed–Sternberg cells.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 607

questions.stem: Copy-number gains of which proto-oncogene on chromosome 2p are common in Hodgkin lymphoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Copy-number gains in the REL proto-oncogene on chromosome 2p are particularly common in Hodgkin's lymphoma. It may also contribute to increased NF-Κβ activity.

Reed-Sternberg cells are aneuploid and possess diverse clonal chromosomal aberrations.

Note: the MYC gene, commonly associated with Burkitt lymphoma is present on chromosome 8. 





Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page: 612

questions.stem: In which of the following lesions can we see the Reed-Sternberg-like cells?
questions.solutionHtml:
Reed–Sternberg-like cells (RSLC) can be seen in the following:

  • Infectious mononucleosis 
  • Large-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (most common in immunoblastic NHL)
  • Solid tissue cancers

While Reed-Sternberg cells (RS cells) are seen in Hodgkin’s lymphoma, there can be presence of Reed-Sternberg like cells which that may have morphologic features resembling RS cells.

Diagnostic Reed–Sternberg cells are large cells with multiple nuclei or a single nucleus with multiple nuclear lobes, each with a large inclusion-like nucleolus, about the size of a small lymphocyte with abundant cytoplasm (owl-eye appearance).

The image given below shows the classic Reed Sternberg cells.







Robbins Basic Pathology, 10e, Page no. 612
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK542333/
Online Resource, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3812872/#:~:text=The%20presence%20of%20Reed%2DSternberg,Hodgkin's%20lymphoma%20can%20be%20encountered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a variant of the Reed-Sternberg cell?
questions.solutionHtml:
Monomorphic is not a variant of RS cell.

Reed–Sternberg cell (RS cell) is the characteristic tumor giant cell of Hodgkin Lymphoma. It is derived from the germinal center B cell. It has a classic owl-eyed appearance due to the presence of a symmetric or mirror-image bilobed nucleus, with prominent nucleoli surrounded by a clear space. It has the following variants:

  • Lacunar
  • Classic 
  • L&H Popcorn cells 
  • Pleomorphic
  • Mononuclear

RS cells should be present in a background of non-neoplastic inflammatory cells like lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils, to make a diagnosis of Hodgkin’s lymphoma.

The image given below shows the diagnostic Reed-Sternberg cell, with two nuclear lobes, large inclusion-like nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm, surrounded by lymphocytes, macrophages, and an eosinophil.



The image below shows Reed-Sternberg cell, mononuclear variant.



The image below shows Reed-Sternberg cell, lacunar variant. This variant has a folded or multilobated nucleus and lies within an open space, which is an artefact created by disruption of the cytoplasm during tissue sectioning.



The image below shows the Reed-Sternberg cell, lymphohistiocytic variant. Several such variants with multiple infolded nuclear membranes, small nucleoli, fine chromatin, and abundant pale cytoplasm are present.









Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 608

questions.stem: A patient with generalized lymphadenopathy and Pel-Ebstein fever is diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma. Which of the following is a characteristic finding seen in this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Pain in nodes relieved by alcohol

options.label: B
options.text: Pain in nodes aggravated by alcohol

questions.answerText: Pain in nodes aggravated by alcohol
questions.solutionHtml:
In the case of Hodgkin's Lymphoma, the pain in the lymph nodes aggravates following the intake of alcohol.

Clinical features of HL:

  • Painless enlargement of lymph nodes is the most common presenting symptom.
  • Cyclical fever (Pel–Ebstein fever) - cyclical increase, which then decreases over an average period of one or two weeks and night sweats in disseminated disease. This cyclical fever may be due to the release of cytokines.

A unique paraneoplastic syndrome associated with Hodgkin's lymphoma is the occurrence of pain in the affected lymph nodes during alcohol consumption. This has been attributed to the enlargement of the affected lymph nodes following alcohol consumption, which stretches the capsule of the lymph node and produces pain.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no 610
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1010854/pdf/westjmed00202-0092.pdf

questions.stem: A lymph node biopsy sample of a patient showed Reed-Sternberg cells that were CD15 & CD30 negative. Which of the variants of Hodgkin lymphoma is the patient most likely to have?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario with biopsy findings of CD15 and CD30 negative Reed–Sternberg cell is suggestive of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.

The Reed–Sternberg cells are positive for CD15 and CD30 for most subtypes, except in lymphocyte-predominant HL, in which the neoplastic cells stains for CD20 and BCL-6.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 607

questions.stemHtml: Which subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma has an incidence as shown in the graph given below?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given graph shows a disease with a biphasic incidence which is characteristically seen in mixed cellularity type of Hodgkin lymphoma.

It has a male predominance, biphasic incidence, peaking in young adults and again in adults older than 55 years. It has more systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss. There is diffuse involvement of the entire lymph node.  It consists of a mixture of cells composed of T cells, eosinophils, plasma cells, and benign macrophages mixed with Reed–Sternberg cells. The mononuclear variant and diagnostic Reed–Sternberg cells are seen in this type.

Reed–Sternberg cell is infected with Epstein–Barr virus in 70% of cases. It has very good prognosis. 

Image given below shows mononuclear variant of RS cell.






Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page no 612, 613
WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues - 2017, Page no 440

questions.stem: Which subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma is associated with older age, systemic symptoms, and advanced tumor stage?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mixed-cellularity Hodgkin's lymphoma is associated with older age, systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss, and advanced tumor stage.

It has a biphasic incidence peaking in young adults and again in adults more than 55 years of age. It also has a strong association with HIV. It is more common in males than females.

Nonetheless, the overall prognosis is very good.





Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page no. 612
WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues - 2017, Page 440

questions.stemHtml: The given histological findings were noted on a lymph node biopsy of a patient with lymphadenopathy. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given image shows a lacunar variant of Reed–Sternberg cell. These are common in the nodular sclerosis subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma.

Subtypes of Hodgkin's lymphoma along with their characteristic types of RS cells is given below:

Hodgkin lymphoma (subtypes) Diagnostic cells in histology Immunophenotype
Nodular sclerosis Lacunar variant CD 15+, CD 30 +
Mixed cellularity 

Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells  (70% EBV +)

CD 15+, CD 30 +
Lymphocyte Rich

Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells  (40% EBV +)

CD 15+, CD 30 + 
Lymphocyte Depletion Reticular variant; (most EBV+) CD 15+, CD 30 +
Lymphocyte predominance Lymphocytic and histiocytic variant, popcorn cells (EBV -)

CD 20+, BCL6+ 

CD 15 -, CD 30 -

 



The image given below shows nodular sclerosis type of HL with lacunar cells.






Robbins Basic Pathology, 10th Edition, Page no 475
Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no 609

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false regarding the nodular sclerosis variant of Hodgkin lymphoma?

options.label: A
options.text: Reed-Sternberg cells are positive for PAX 5

options.label: B
options.text: It is uncommonly associated with Epstein Barr Virus

options.label: D
options.text: Reed-Sternberg cells are positive for CD45

questions.answerText: Reed-Sternberg cells are positive for CD45
questions.solutionHtml:
Reed–Sternberg cells in nodular sclerosis variant of Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) are negative for CD45. It is the most common variant.

These are characterized by the presence of lacunar variant Reed–Sternberg cells and the deposition of collagen bands. These bands divide involved lymph nodes into circumscribed nodules.

The Reed-Sternberg cells are found in a polymorphous background of T cells, eosinophils, plasma cells, and macrophages. Diagnostic Reed-Sternberg cells are often uncommon.

The Reed–Sternberg cells are positive for PAX5 (a B-cell transcription factor), CD15, and CD30, and negative for other B-cell markers, T-cell markers, and CD45 (leukocyte common antigen). This subtype is uncommonly associated with Epstein–Barr virus (EBV).

Involvement of the spleen, liver, bone marrow and other organs and tissues can occur later in the disease. 

The prognosis is excellent.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 608
Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page no.: 612

questions.stem: Lymph node biopsy of which of the following variants of Hodgkin lymphoma will show the maximum area of necrosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
The lymphocyte-depleted subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma is associated with maximum necrosis of the lymph nodes.

Lymphocyte-depleted is the least common type (<5%). It is seen in older and HIV-infected individuals and can present with systemic symptoms. There is a paucity of lymphocytes and a relative abundance of Reed–Sternberg (RS) cells or their pleomorphic variants. RS cells are CD15+ and CD30+ RS cells are infected with Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) in 90% of the cases. It has a poor prognosis.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no 609

questions.stem: Which subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma is most commonly associated with HIV?
questions.solutionHtml:
The Mixed cellularity subtype of Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL) is most commonly associated with HIV.

Note: Although both mixed cellularity and lymphocyte depletion are seen in patients with HIV, mixed cellularity is more commonly associated with HIV.





Williams Hematology 9th Edition, Page no: 1609
WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues - 2017, Page no 440
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page no: 852
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8430611/

questions.stemHtml: A 15-year-old male patient came to the OPD with cervical lymph node enlargement. The biopsy was examined, which showed a variant of the Reed-Sternberg cell given in the image. Which of the following types of Hodgkin's lymphoma frequently has this cell in its histology?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given image shows the lymphohistiocytic variant (L&H) of Reed–Sternberg (RS) cell. It is seen frequently in lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma.

The cell has the following features:

  • Polypoid nuclei
  • Inconspicuous nucleoli
  • Moderately abundant cytoplasm  

As it resembles popcorn in its morphology it is also termed popcorn cell.

Note: A unique paraneoplastic syndrome associated with Hodgkin's lymphoma is the occurrence of pain in the affected lymph nodes during alcohol consumption. This has been attributed to the enlargement of the affected lymph nodes following alcohol consumption, which stretches the capsule of the lymph node and produces pain.





Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page 613, 614

questions.stem: A young male presented with cervical lymphadenopathy. The biopsy of the lymph node showed RS cells with vague nodule formation and a background of reactive T-lymphocytes. The cells were positive for CD20, LCA, EMA and negative for CD 15 and CD30. What is the diagnosis?

options.label: C
options.text: T cell rich B cell lymphoma

questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma (NLPHL).

Axial group (cervical) lymphadenopathy and along with the L&H variant of Reed-Sternberg cells is characteristic.

RS cells are neoplastic giant cells. In NLPHL, the cells have vague nodular formation. Immunophenotyping is positive for CD20 (B cell-associated), LCA (CD45), EMA (epithelial marker), and negative for CD15 (monocyte or macrophage-associated) and CD30 (activation marker).

The image given below shows the L&H variant of RS cells seen in NLPHL.






Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page 609

questions.stem: In a patient with lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, cells are found to be positive for which of the following marker?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nodular-lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin Lymphomas have Reed Sternberg cells(aka L&H CELL) that are BCL-6 positive & CD 20 positive and CD 15 & CD 30 negative.

Note:

  • CD30 is the most sensitive marker of Reed–Sternberg cell.
  • PAX5 is the most specific marker of Reed–Sternberg cell.




Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page: 613, 614

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma?

options.label: A
options.text: It can progress to a tumor resembling DLBCL

options.label: C
options.text: The bone marrow involvement is rare

options.label: D
options.text: A strong association with EBV is seen

questions.answerText: A strong association with EBV is seen
questions.solutionHtml:
Lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL) is not associated with Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) infection.

In 3% to 5% of cases, this type transforms into a tumor resembling diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

A majority of patients are males, usually younger than 35 years of age, who typically present with cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy. Mediastinal and bone marrow involvement is rare.

This form of HL is more likely to recur than the classical subtypes, but the prognosis is excellent.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 609
WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues - 2017, Page no. 433

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man is diagnosed to have Stage II (A) Hodgkin's lymphoma. What staging system was most likely used to classify the tumor of this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Clinical staging of both Hodgkin and Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is done by Ann-Arbor classification. 

Option B: Masaoka staging is used for thymoma.

Option C: Modified Durie–Salmon staging is used for multiple myeloma. 

 





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no.611

questions.stem: Who among the following patients is likely to have the best prognosis?

options.label: A
options.text: A patient with mononuclear variant of Reed-Sternberg cells on lymph node biopsy

options.label: B
options.text: A patient whose lymph node biopsy showed lacunar Reed-Sternberg cells

options.label: C
options.text: A patient with predominant reticular variant of Reed- Sternberg cells

options.label: D
options.text: A patient with Reed-Sternberg cells amid mixed variety of background cells

questions.answerText: A patient whose lymph node biopsy showed lacunar Reed-Sternberg cells
questions.solutionHtml:
The prognosis of the nodular sclerosis ( a subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma) is excellent compared to the other subtypes mentioned in the options. Lacunar Reed-Sternberg cells are seen in this condition.

The nodular sclerosis type occurs with equal frequency in males and females. It has a propensity to involve the lower cervical, supraclavicular, and mediastinal lymph nodes of adolescents or young adults.

Subtypes of Hodgkin's lymphoma along with their characteristic types of RS cells is given below:

Hodgkin lymphoma (subtypes) Diagnostic cells in histology Immunophenotype
Nodular sclerosis Lacunar variant CD 15+, CD 30 +
Mixed cellularity 

Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells  (70% EBV +)

CD 15+, CD 30 +
Lymphocyte Rich

Mononuclear and Diagnostic RS cells  (40% EBV -)

CD 15+, CD 30 + 
Lymphocyte Depletion Reticular variant; (most EBV+) CD 15+, CD 30 +
Lymphocyte predominance Lymphocytic and histiocytic variant, popcorn cells (EBV -)

CD 20+, BCL6+ 

CD 15 -, CD 30 -

Nodular lymphocyte-predominant non-classical Hodgkin lymphoma also has an excellent prognosis.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no.608-610
WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues - 2017, Page no 437

questions.stem: Which among the following is incorrect about Hodgkin's lymphoma?

options.label: A
options.text: Histologic type is the most important prognostic variable.

options.label: B
options.text: The cure rate of patients with stages I and IIA is close to 90%.

options.label: C
options.text: Long-term survivors treated with radiotherapy had a much higher incidence of secondary malignancies.

options.label: D
options.text: It most commonly presents as painless lymphadenopathy.

questions.answerText: Histologic type is the most important prognostic variable.
questions.solutionHtml:
With current treatment protocols, the tumor stage is the most important prognostic variable, not histologic type.

Hodgkin's Lymphoma most commonly presents as painless lymphadenopathy.

The cure rate of patients with stages I and IIA are close to 90%.

Long-term survivors treated with radiotherapy had a much higher incidence of certain malignancies, such as lung cancer, melanoma, and breast cancer.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no. 610

questions.stem: Which listed finding is an adverse factor in the original seven-factor International Prognostic Score for advanced Hodgkin lymphoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct answer: C - Absolute lymphocyte count below 600/mm3

C is correct. The original IPS includes lymphocytes below 600/mm3 or below 8% of the white cell count. Its other factors are albumin below 4 g/dL, hemoglobin below 10.5 g/dL, male sex, age at least 45, stage IV and white cells at least 15,000/mm3. The imported albumin threshold below 5 g/dL overlapped the true adverse range and was not a clean distractor. This is a historically specified prognostic score, not an individual outcome prediction. Seven retained micrographs illustrate Hodgkin cell morphology and do not establish the laboratory thresholds.
